hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: The Midwest is often called America's heartland. With its traditional ((values)) of conservatism, ambition and self-sufficiency, it represents the most “mainstream” image of the USA.

Situated in the Interior ((Plains)), the land is flat and fertile—excellent ((conditions)) for farming. Corn, soybeans, wheat and other ((crops)) are grown here in large amounts. This makes the Midwest the center of American ((agriculture)).

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>fertile</lang> bedeutet fruchtbar, <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>sparsely populated</lang> bedeutet dünn bevölkert
hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: Apart from farming, manufacturing used to play a big part in Midwestern economy, especially the steel industry. However, with the decline of the manufacturing ((industry)) since the late 20th century, many factories ((closed)) and the workers lost their jobs.

The Midwestern population is predominantly White. Although most of its states lean towards ((Republicans)), the Midwest includes some swing states which do not consistently favour one ((party)) over the other throughout elections.
The population concentrates in big cities and around the ((Great_Lakes)) in the region's East, while the vast ((countryside)) is only sparsely populated.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The Midwestern population is not very racially diverse.
The Midwest's terrain is flat with no mountain ranges.
The Midwest is situated by the Great Lakes.
Most Midwestern people value liberal and progressive virtues.

wrong.text: Despite some swing states, Midwesterners generally tend to be conservative.

atoms.a: The population is much denser in the countryside than in urban areas.

wrong.text: It is the other way around: Urban areas are more densely populated than the countryside.

atoms.b: The West makes up about half the area of the entire US. The region is marked by the ((Rocky_Mountains)), as well as several smaller mountain ranges further west. Cities in the coastal states are densely populated, while the population in the ((inland)) is rather sparse in comparison. Alaska and ((Hawaii)), the two states that do not share borders with the rest of the US, also belong to the Western states.

While the Pacific Northwest has a temperate climate, the Southern regions have hot summers and mild ((winters)). The pine forests of Washington are a stark contrast to Arizona's desert — not to mention Alaska's snowy mountains and the ((tropical)) temperatures in Hawaii.

The West, especially California, is a hot spot for entertainment and innovation. Hollywood, a part of Los Angeles, is the heart and soul of the ((film)) industry, while Silicon Valley around San Francisco Bay is the center of many major ((tech)) companies.

Furthermore, the West has the largest number of minorities overall. In comparison to the other regions, it has the biggest populations of Native, Asian, and Hispanic or ((Latin)) Americans. While almost all Pacific States value equality and liberalism, some of the Mountain States prefer the Democrats, some the ((Republicans)), and a few of them are swing states.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The West is the biggest region in the US.
The population density in the West varies between the coast and inland.
Political attitudes throughout the West are diverse.
The entire West has a tropical climate.

wrong.text: Hawaii is the only Western state with a tropical climate. The rest ranges from hot to rather cold temperatures.

atoms.a: Few racial minorities live in the West.

wrong.text: The West has the largest number of racial minorities of all US regions.

atoms.a: California's economy relies strongly on agriculture.

wrong.text: California's economy focuses mainly on technical innovation and media.

atoms.a: The West is located by the Atlantic coast.

wrong.text: It is located by the Pacific coast.
